figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Illustrative example highlighting the importance of fidelity check for tabular data structure. ❶: A real-world physical system showing the gravitational forces acting on ball A. The system is described by ball density (ρ), volume (V ), masses (mA & mB ), distance (r), and gravitational forces (Fball & FEarth ). For simplicity, we assume both balls share identical density. ❷: We derive the ground-truth (GT) causal structure of the system based on Newton’s law of universal gravitation. ❸: We interpret the encoded physical laws of the system as the conditional independence (CI) across variables. ❹: We evaluate four generators by conventional metrics. ❺: We assess the structural fidelity by CI tests and the proposed global utility metric. We note that the global structure reflects full conditional independence across all variables, while the local structure includes only those directly relevant to a specific prediction task at hand (Fball ). Results demonstrate that conventional metrics are insufficient: for instance, while SMOTE is able to outperform other generators on conventionally used dimensions (e.g., ML efficacy) – the generated synthetic data only preserves local structure and violates most physical laws. For tabular data, where the truthfulness and authenticity of synthetic data is hard to verify, global utility provides an effective mechanism for evaluating the alignment of the synthetic data to the likely ground-truth causal structure.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: The visual narrative starts with Figure 1’s physical-law counterexample and Figure 2’s benchmark scope, then establishes coverage in Table 1 and the main aggregate decision surface in Table 2. Figure 3 turns complementarity and local/global alignment into a heatmap-plus-scatter, Figure 4 adds practical cost, and Appendix Figures 5–9 connect split design, rank stability, feature-level mechanism categories, predictor robustness, and independent-set behavior to the same benchmark claims. Tables 3–9 define the dataset/model universe, Tables 10–21 expose reproducibility settings, Tables 22–37 test extensions and sensitivities, and Tables 38–66 restore per-dataset raw evidence.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions generally begin with a bold short title and then provide setup, comparison, and selected interpretation. Main Figure 3 and Table 2 captions state their headline relation; Figure 4 and Tables 22–37 add selective uncertainty/p-value or appendix pointers. Raw tables repeat a long caption that defines mean ± std, first/second/third highlighting, CI abbreviation, and the local/global generator-family interpretation. Captions do not uniformly define error-bar/band statistics or all denominators, so surrounding prose remains necessary.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: The main metric tables use a two-level grouped header: generator rows followed by Density Estimation, Privacy Preservation, ML Efficacy, and Structural Fidelity subcolumns. Scope tables switch to nested classification/regression or generator-category headers; registries use descriptive metadata columns; hyperparameter tables use a flat Hyperparameter/Range header; compact appendix analyses use outcome-column or condition-by-metric headers. The fixed generator/metric order across Table 2 and Tables 38–66 is the strongest cross-object header contract.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 supplies the conceptual structural-fidelity mechanism and Figure 2 defines the benchmark interface; Figure 5 fixes the split protocol. Table 2 and Figure 3 quantify metric complementarity and global/local alignment. Figure 6, Table 24/25, and Figure 8 test ranking stability; Figure 7 and Tables 32–37 supply mechanism/robustness slices; Table 31 is the explicit GReaT column-order controlled variant; Figure 9 is a split-variant check rather than a component ablation. No conventional named component-ablation section is present.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–2 carry the paper’s decision spine. Appendix Tables 3–9 define scope and datasets; Tables 10–21 document tuning; Tables 22–37 extend metric validity, confounding, causal inference, availability, and formulation robustness; Tables 38–66 provide raw per-dataset values. Appendix Figures 5–9 are explicitly called by the main text or Appendix E and close protocol, mechanism, and robustness gaps without changing the main metric grammar.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: The surrounding paper and tables predominantly use Nimbus Roman/Times-like text with Computer Modern math; PDF font objects also expose Calibri/Aptos/Cambria Math in embedded figure/material components. Table typography is more consistent and usually high-confidence from PDF objects, while figure-internal labels are smaller and mixed sans/serif. The appendix’s wide tables and 21-panel Figure 7 operate near the lower readable limit.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Green/red binary marks and teal/purple/orange rank text are reused in tables, while plot families use separate categorical palettes. Blue/orange carries reference-versus-synthetic or independent-set semantics in Figures 5 and 9; blue lines/bands encode utility in Figure 7; generator hues are repeated in Figures 6 and 8. The semantics are locally consistent but not globally uniform, and grayscale safety is limited.

most_reusable_patterns: A numbered physical-law → causal-graph → CI → metric-failure chain that makes structural fidelity concrete.
A fixed grouped metric header and generator order reused from the aggregate Table 2 through all 29 raw tables.
Paired local/global correlation, scatter, and rank-line views that distinguish target-local utility from holistic structure.
Condition-by-metric robustness tables and paired variant rows for sample size, predictor configuration, latent confounding, and column order.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 p.2, because it converts the central abstract gap into a self-contained causal/evaluation mechanism.
Table 2 p.8, because it puts four evaluation dimensions and SCM/real-world regimes on one decision surface.
Figure 3 p.9, because the heatmap and utility scatter jointly expose complementarity and local/global bias.
Figure 7 p.43, because it restores feature-level evidence behind aggregate global-utility claims.
failure_patterns: Wide tables and multi-panel figures push labels near the minimum readable size.
Color-based first/second/third, check/cross, and generator identity encodings are not consistently grayscale-safe.
Aggregate means/ranks hide per-dataset heterogeneity unless the reader follows the long Appendix F raw-table series.
Captions often state a conclusion but leave error-bar/band definitions, denominators, tie handling, and selected configurations to surrounding prose.
Appendix E includes useful controlled variants but no single component-ablation matrix; the GReaT order test is the clearest one-factor intervention.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Make structural-fidelity claims legible by anchoring them in a physical/causal worked example, keeping a fixed metric-by-generator table grammar, and using paired correlation, rank, feature-level, and cost views to connect aggregate decisions to mechanism and robustness evidence.
